title: Joining the DeLisa in 1937 and taking over the band
summary: Albert Ammons had just left, Dell Bright led the six-piece band then went to Horace Henderson, and Saunders took over around late 1937.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Well, when did you go into the Delésá?
I went into the Delésá in '37.

No. When I first went into the Delésá, Albert Ammons had just left, see, and they let him go because he couldn't play -- he couldn't read, see, and shows and things got the best of him. And then right after that, John Hammond -- he and --
Lux and T. Johnson, teamed them up, [Delbert] and a boy by the name of Dell Bright was the saxophone player.

Yeah, so he had the band. And I stayed there about -- oh, six months or nine months, and then Dell went to work with Horace Henderson at the Swingland, and he went there because -- I guess he wanted a big band thing,

and Horace had a big band and we had only six pieces there. So he turned the band over to me. So I took the band over there, then in 19-- well, I guess about '37, '38, because I'd been there about -- the last part of '37, I think it was. And that's when I took the band over there.
It was a small band. We had only six men, trumpet, tenor, alto, bass, piano and drums, right.
